en: The Sūtra on Ānanda’s Fellow Students, as spoken by the Buddha, extracted from the Ekottarika Āgama, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.

At that time, in the city of Śrāvastī, there was a bhikṣu named Kūṭadanta, who had been a fellow student with the Venerable Ānanda since childhood. He held him in great love, respect, and affection, and they were very close, never having been angry with one another; yet he did not delight in practicing the holy life and wished to relinquish the precepts to return to the status of a layman.
At that time, Ānanda went to where the World-Honored One was; having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
Then Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

“In this city of Śrāvastī, there is a bhikṣu named Kūṭadanta, who was my fellow student from childhood. He is unable to cultivate the holy life and wishes to relinquish the precepts to return to the status of a layman.”
“May the Blessed One teach the Dharma to the bhikṣu Khujja, so that he may practice the holy life with purity in this very life!
Then, the Blessed One addressed Ānanda: “Ānanda!...”
"You should go yourself to where that bhikṣu Ghoṭaka is.
He replied, "So be it."
"World-Honored One!
Ānanda, having received the instruction from the Buddha, went to where the bhikṣu Khujjuttara was.
"The World-Honored One summons you? he asked.
He replied, "So be it.
Then, following Ānanda’s instruction, the bhikṣu Khujjuttara went to where the World-Honored One was. Upon arrival, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and sat down to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣu Khujja, saying:
"Bhikṣu, is it true that you do not delight in practicing the holy life, and wish to abandon the precepts to return to the state of a layman?"
The bhikṣu replied:
“Indeed it is so, World-Honored One! And why is this so?”
"With body aflame and mind aflame, one is incapable of practicing the pure holy life.
The Blessed One said: "Monk!"
Women have five types of defiled conduct.
What are these five? Bhikṣus!
Women are foul and impure; their speech is coarse and vulgar, and they lack a heart of reciprocity. They are like venomous snakes that constantly harbor poisonous filth.
These women increase the hosts of Māra and are difficult to liberate, being like iron hooks and chains.
Women should not be approached, for they are like poisoned food that must not be eaten;
women cannot be digested, just as a vajra destroys and ruins the human body.
O Bhikṣu!
They are also like a flame, just like that Avīci hell. Bhikṣus!
A woman is not to be scrutinized, for she is like stinking excrement.
"Monks! Women are not to be listened to; they are like the sound of death. Monks!"
Women are like a prison, just like the Vemacitra prison where the Asuras are bound;
monks! Women are enemies, like venomous snakes; monks, you should keep far away from them, as one would from evil associates.
"Monks! Women are a source of terror, like a village of bandits. Monks!"
A human body is difficult to obtain, like the udumbara flower;
O Bhikṣu!
A human body is extremely difficult to obtain, like a board with a single hole that, when pushed into the water, happens to align with its hole only after tens of thousands of years.
"Monks! Time is also difficult to encounter, except for eight specific times.
You monks, having already obtained this human body, have all achieved it through the deeds performed in previous lives."
“Monks! A Buddha, a World-Honored One, appears in the world only rarely and is difficult to encounter, just as a barren woman has no son. Monks!”
The appearance of a Tathāgata in the world is extremely difficult to encounter, just like the udumbara flower.

Bhikṣus! You have already obtained a human body, you have already received full ordination, and you have also gained entry into the assembly; you are like those favored by a noble king. Furthermore, for the sake of others I preach the Dharma, teaching the practice of śamatha and vipaśyanā until reaching the realm of Nirvāṇa. Having reached that state, the Tathāgata has well-expounded this Dharma.
"O bhikṣu, cultivate the pure brahmacarya; you shall bring an end to the source of suffering.
At that time, having received this instruction from the Buddha, that bhikṣu, while still on his seat, attained the purity of the Dharma-eye, free from dust and defilement.
Then, that bhikṣu rose from his seat, bowed his head at the feet of the World-Honored One, and withdrew.
At that time, having heard this instruction from the World-Honored One, the bhikṣu went to a secluded place to enjoy himself in solitude.

Dwelling in a secluded and tranquil place, he finds joy therein; thus, the son of noble family has shaved off his hair and beard, donned the saffron robes, and practiced the unsurpassed holy life under the Tathāgata. Having reached the end of the source of birth and death, his holy life is established, what was to be done has been accomplished, and he shall no longer receive a mother’s womb.
At that time, that bhikṣu immediately became an arhat.
Then, the Venerable Khujjuttara went to where the Blessed One was; having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and sat down to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Kūṭadanta addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"Blessed One!
I have now regained awareness of your instructions; I pray that the Blessed One grant me leave to enter parinirvāṇa!"
At that time, the World-Honored One remained silent and did not respond.
The Venerable Bhikṣu Kūṭadanta addressed the World-Honored One a second and a third time, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"What you were taught has now been fully realized; I pray that the World-Honored One will grant me permission to enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One said to him, "Bhikṣu!"
"Now is precisely the right time.
That bhikṣu immediately rose from his seat, prostrated with his head at [the Buddha's] feet, circumambulated the World-Honored One three times, and then withdrew to depart, returning to his own cell.
Having arrived, he set aside his sitting mat and spread it upon the open ground; then, ascending into the air, he manifested various transformations:
he would transform a single body into many bodies, or many bodies into a single body;

he would become stone or iron, or diamond (*vajra*), or become walls, ramparts, and city gates, or high mountains and rocky cliffs—passing through all these without obstruction—and emerging from or sinking into the earth as freely as flowing water, without hindrance.
Sitting cross-legged, they filled the void of space; like great blazing flames, like soaring birds, and like the sun and moon, they possessed great majestic power and mighty strength.

With their hands they stroked and rubbed themselves, transforming their bodies to reach as far as the Brahma Heaven. Within the void of space, they sat, lay down, and walked back and forth. They sometimes manifested smoke and flames: smoke issued from the lower part of their bodies while fire issued from the upper part; fire issued from the upper part of their bodies while smoke issued from the lower part; smoke issued from the left side while fire issued from the right; fire issued from the left side while smoke issued from the right; smoke issued from the front while flames issued from the rear; flames issued from the front while smoke issued from the rear; smoke issued from their entire bodies, flames issued from their entire bodies, and fire issued from their entire bodies.

Then, that bhikṣu withdrew his supernormal powers and sat alone; folding his legs crosswise, he straightened his body and set his mind upright, fixing his mindfulness before him, and entered the first dhyāna.

Emerging from the first dhyāna, he enters the second dhyāna; emerging from the second dhyāna, he enters the third dhyāna; emerging from the third dhyāna, he enters the fourth dhyāna; emerging from the fourth dhyāna, he enters the sphere of infinite space; emerging from the sphere of infinite space, he enters the sphere of infinite consciousness; emerging from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he enters the sphere of nothingness; emerging from the sphere of nothingness, he enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters the samādhi of the cessation of perception and feeling.

Emerging from the samādhi of the cessation of perception and feeling, he enters the spheres of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, nothingness, infinite consciousness, infinite space, the fourth dhyāna, the third dhyāna, the second dhyāna, and the first dhyāna.
Again, emerging from the first dhyāna, he enters the second dhyāna and the third dhyāna.
At that time, the Venerable Kūṭadanta arose from the fourth dhyāna and, relinquishing his body and life, entered parinirvāṇa in the realm of nirvana without remainder.

Then, Ānanda made offerings to the relics of the Venerable Kūṭadanta and went to where the World-Honored One was; having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

"As for that bhikṣu Khujjuttara, having received instruction from the Tathāgata, he delights himself in a secluded place. For this reason, a son of good family has shaved off his hair and beard, donned the three dharma-robes, and with firm faith has left the home life to study the Path. He has cultivated the unsurpassed holy life, exhausted the source of birth and death, established the holy life, accomplished what was to be done, and shall no longer receive a mother’s womb."
“World-Honored One!
That venerable Kūṭadanta has already entered parinirvāṇa.
The World-Honored One replied:
"How marvelous, how extraordinary! Ānanda!
The Buddha, the World-Honored One, has accomplished immeasurable wisdom, such that he is able to enable the bhikṣu Ghoṭamukha to cross over the abyss of birth and death."

"Ānanda, this is so because the Tathāgata’s practice is already complete; how much more so, then, regarding his deliverance of countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings from the abyss of birth and death, and his further rescue of those yet to be saved?"
Therefore, Ānanda,
you should give rise to this intention toward the Buddha, the Dharma,
and the Saṅgha. Thus it is, Ānanda!
"You should train yourself in this way.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on Ānanda’s Shared Training* as spoken by the Buddha.
